div.l: His breed his ale was alway after on
A better envyned man / was the nowher noon
Vith oute bake mete / was neuyr his hous
Of Fyssh of flessh / and that so plentevous
It sewed in his hows / of mete and drynk
Of alle deyntees / that men cowde thynke
After the sondry sesoıı̄uns / of the yere
So changed he his mete / and his sopere
Wel many a fat ꝑpertrych / had he in mewe
And many a breme / and many a luce in stewe
Woo was his cook / but yif his sauce were
Poynaıı̄unt and redy / al his other gere
His table dormānt / in his halle alway
Stod redy keueryd / al the longe day
At sessioıı̄uns / ther was he lorde and syre
Wel oftyn tyme / he was knyht of the shyre
An Anlas and a gysper / al of sylk
Heng at his gerdel / white as morwe mylk
A shereve had he be / and a comptour
Was nowher such / a worthy vavasoure

An Habirdasshere
A Carpenter
A Wever
A Dyer
A TapistereAN habirdasshere / and a Carpenteer
A Webber a dyere / and a Tapistere
And they were clothed / Alle in oon lyvere
Of a solempne / and a greet fraternyte
Ful froyssh and newe / here gere piked was
Here knyves were nat / chaped with bras
But Al with sylver / wrowt ful clene and wel
Here girdelys / and here powches everydel
Wel seemed eche of hem / A fayr burgeys
To sytten in a yelde halle / or at the deys
Euerich of the wysdam / that he can
Was shaply for to be / a Aldyrman
For catel hadde they I now / and rente
